title: What customers actually saw
lede: Pages as saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, stored here as images; click one to open the original capture. We found the captures through the CDX API in October 2026.[^38]

snips.text: “There’s never been a better time to be a Toys“R”Us kid”
“Shop online at Toysrus.com, teamed with amazon.com”
“Visit the Center of the Toy Universe: Toys“R”Us Times Square, New York”
“Thanks to each of you who shared your amazing journey to (and through) parenthood with us… Promise us just this one thing: Don’t ever grow up. Play on!”
“Got some questions? We have answers for you in our Store Closing FAQ.”

note: Home page captures from 1998 and 1999 exist but their images were never archived, and a February 2001 capture of the bare domain resolves to an unrelated site, so they are not shown. The footer of the July 2018 page reads “© 2018 Geoffrey, LLC,” the subsidiary that held the trademarks.

captures.label: The Amazon years
captures.title: A front door to someone else’s store
captures.text: The company’s own site was a brochure: store locator, investor relations, a baby registry. Shopping happened at a co-branded store run by Amazon, reached by the button at top right.

captures.label: Three months before
captures.title: Three months before the filing
captures.text: A full online store, with a Babies“R”Us link above the header. The pop-up asking for an email address is part of the original page.
captures.warn: The capture’s own sign-up pop-up covers part of the page.

captures.label: Play on
captures.title: The farewell
captures.text: Three days after the last stores closed, the store was gone from the site. What remained was a thank-you note, a store closing FAQ and a page on the company’s history.
